result:
Yes — this breaks the exact guarantee you just built the approval gate to provide. If gofmt/goimports commit changes *after* the diff hash is logged, that hash no longer matches what actually merges. If a release gets questioned, you can't point to "this hash is what was approved and what shipped" anymore — you can only say "this hash is what was approved, and then something else ran."

Two other risks worth naming: goimports can silently drop an unused import that was actually there for its side effect (e.g. `_ "net/http/pprof"`), which is a real behavior change, not just whitespace; and "Marcus tried it once" doesn't establish safety for a process whose whole point is auditability, not just passing tests.

Better fix: run the formatter as a blocking pre-approval check (CI fails / approval can't be requested until the branch is formatted) so the hash recorded at approval time is already final — no post-approval commits at all. If you want to keep the auto-commit-after-approval flow for convenience anyway, at minimum log it as a distinct event with its own diff hash and don't let it silently supersede the approved hash. I'd hold this out of today's cut unless you go with the pre-approval-check version — happy to help wire that up instead if you want it fast.
